name: Tire Swing

Instead of stitching together 15 disconnected SaaS tools, teams run engineering, product, growth, sales, finance, legal, recruiting, support, and executive operations on a single autonomous agent runtime backed by full Linux sandboxes and a shared company memory map.

name: GodHands

name: Degla Inc

You state the goal, Degla figures out how.

name: Collar
long_description:
We are a team of ex-intelligence, ex-finance, and most importantly, ex-founders who have known each other for over 5 years.

Collar is redefining investor relations. 

Right now, investor relations is an under-appreciated yet sweeping function. 
They have a bird’s eye view of what external stakeholders want, and also work with internal business units to create a grand vision of a company’s future.

But they’re doing it with their hands tied behind their back.

Finance AI tools today are built for investors not investor relations, leaving teams using ad-hoc unreliable workarounds, and CFOs are stuck always reporting rather than acting on insights to optimize operational workstreams.

Before earning calls, Collar prepares CFOs through proactive earnings calls prep, investor targeting and fully citation-backed live teleprompters, saving them hours of work.

After earning calls, CFOs use Collar’s trusted agentic AI systems to optimize identified underperforming workstreams with little manual modification needed. 

Redefining investor relations from a tedious cost centre headache, into a whole-of-company profit maximising function.

name: Nxtcure Labs
long_description:
Reinventing medicine from lab to drug discovery.
NxtCure CRO- an AI-native, full-stack CRO built to take therapeutics from discovery to market faster.
NxtCure Cancer- the all-in-one mobile platform guiding patients through the cancer journey.
We’re building the operating system for the future of medicine.

name: Rodeo Robotics
long_description:
Rodeo builds a robotic technician that automates maintenance so fleets can get vehicles back on the road sooner. Initial deployments focus on oil changes at centralized depots, where routine maintenance competes for scarce technician time.

Cofounders Michael Hazard and Colby Duke met at Applied Intuition, where they worked with OEMs like Toyota and General Motors to bring software and autonomy to vehicles. They saw firsthand how much manual work it takes to keep vehicle fleets running, and learned how to make autonomy reliable through structured testing, real-world data, and human intervention.

They’re now applying their experience to the roughly $600B annual US vehicle maintenance market. The average US vehicle is older than ever, driving up maintenance demand at a time when shops already struggle to hire and retain technicians. That gap leaves fleets facing costly downtime and preventable breakdowns.

Despite this need, vehicle maintenance has resisted traditional automation. Service information is fragmented and unreliable, and vehicle hardware varies significantly between makes and models. Rodeo builds on advances in robotic foundation models to learn maintenance skills that transfer across vehicles.

Rodeo pairs robots with human technicians who ensure each job is completed correctly, handling work the robots can’t yet perform autonomously. These deployments generate training data for Rodeo’s models through both teleoperation and hand tools augmented to record how technicians work. This lets Rodeo earn revenue while collecting the data needed to automate more of each job and improve margins.
one_liner: Robots for vehicle maintenance.

name: Fire Wallet
long_description:
🔥FIRE WALLET 🔥

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JeXDDegwhgA

TL;DR: Fire Wallet is a fast, end-to-end encrypted, non-custodial stablecoin wallet with built-in payment processing and fiat on/off ramps, built by the team that created MobileCoin, the cryptocurrency inside Signal.

Hey Bookface! We're Josh, Michael, and Manny and we're building Fire Wallet!

🔥Why we built this

Most wallets and payment processors don’t work FOR you. They're slow, route your payments in the way that earns them the most, and they leak your financial life to anyone asking. Worse: every single one hold the keys to your money.

We believe your financial tools should act in your interest and, frankly, that your money should be yours.

 🔥What Fire does

Multi-chain, non-custodial, end-to-end encrypted wallet. 
Your keys, your money, your assets: you are in full control of your funds at all times. 
Least Cost Routing. Every swap and payment takes the cheapest path, not the one that pays a middleman the most.
Self-sovereign payment processing. Send an invoice straight from the wallet. Get paid from your web checkout. No middleman.
Easy fiat on/off ramps. Move stablecoins to USD and back without the pain.
Built for agentic commerce. Manage per-agent sub-wallets for agentic workflows.
Encrypted by default. Protecting you from bad actors and surveillance capitalism.

🔥Early traction

Signed our first major LOI with @Trustboop (founded by Justice Laub of Drone Racing League and Rob Rhinehart of Soylent).

Onboarding our first enterprise customer in ecommerce packaging and marketing, doing about $1.5M/month in volume. They've connected us to 10 more companies in the same vertical at similar volume, roughly a $100M/yr GMV opportunity.

🔥Why us

Josh and Manuel led the creation of MobileCoin, the cryptocurrency in Signal Messenger: $100M+ raised, $1.16B peak valuation, $4B+ peak coin market cap, acquired in 2026.

Michael runs product and design. He's an internationally exhibited artist with two published art books, and he builds sick products.

Manuel runs operations and orchestrates systems that actually work at scale.

🔥Asks

Intros to businesses moving $1M+/month in payments, especially cross-border, ecommerce, and DTC, who want lower fees and more control over their funds.

Strategic partners in fintech and payments interested in integrating our infrastructure.
Tell us what's broken. Reply here or email founders@fire.co.

We're looking for our first 100 customers. If that's you or someone you know, we'd love to talk.
one_liner: Fire Wallet is a privacy-first crypto wallet designed to just work,…

name: Lyon
long_description: Lyon builds private foundation models for banks, insurance companies, and fintechs. Each model learns from the company’s proprietary transactions, payments, clicks, and customer interactions to predict credit, fraud, collections, income, churn, and lifetime value; and runs inside the company’s cloud, so its data and intelligence remain under its control. Lyon is already working with a major insurer and trained a model on 28B transactions for a fintech serving tens of millions of active users, identifying premium-card converters 4x more precisely than its existing rules; the model is now being deployed for credit.
one_liner: Foundation models on enterprise transaction data.

name: Definite
long_description:
Definite is where finance teams build everyday back-office agents on one live model of their books. We plug into your ERP, ledger, payroll, and payments read-only and compile everything into one clean model that stays current as money moves. Your back-office team then builds agents on top in plain English. We never write back and we never move money. The agents are yours, the plumbing is ours.

We met in first year computer science at Waterloo and interned at Meta, Optiver, and BitGo. At Optiver they ran an n8n hackathon and the interns automated basically nothing. It couldn't talk to the systems that mattered. When we pitched banks and fintechs on agents, they kept telling us the same thing. The agent isn't the hard part, getting clean data out of their systems is.

Right now, automating anything in a back office means engineers hand-stitching data from a dozen sources in different formats on different schedules. Tools like n8n and Workato assume your data is already clean and joined. In finance it never is. So the teams with the most repetitive work and smallest budgets get nothing.

The hard part is the compiler. Every source gets cleaned, matched, and joined into one live model of transactions, invoices, vendors, and payments, and it has to stay right as money lands every day. 

Everyone throws engineers at this. We're doing it once so nobody has to again. Every back office is getting agents eventually. Whoever owns the data they read from owns the thing all of them depend on, and eventually the books themselves. That's what we're building.
one_liner: Build everyday back-office agents on one live model of your books

Customers including Airwallex, Worldpay, Citizens Bank, FV Bank and Shopmonkey have used our agents to automate over 250,000 of operational work across compliance, onboarding, underwriting, corporate due diligence, document verification, merchant categorization, market and competitive research, rev ops and much more.

We founded Grep AI after experiencing firsthand how manual workflows can prevent a business from growing when we ran the platform team at Brex. We're now on a mission to rid businesses of tedious, repetitive so their employees can focus on the most high leverage tasks that matter.

name: Hue
long_description: Hue turns production usage of agents into repeatable tests that preserve the tools, data, and state behind the real run. As AI agents take on real work, their behavior depends increasingly on the nuances of the world around them. With Hue, teams can test and improve their agents under conditions that mimic real usage.
one_liner: Test agents in realistic worlds built from production usage

name: herdr
long_description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.
one_liner: building the open agent runtime

name: Sentient OS
long_description:
Nobody's built truly proactive AI, because it requires running inference on your entire life. In the cloud, that's insanely expensive and a privacy nightmare. But not on your own chip.

Every night, Sentient's on-device LLM wakes your Mac and understands what's new in your life (email, messages, files, Granola transcripts...), entirely locally, and distills it into a knowledge base.

You wake up to your work already prepared: the reply you forgot, drafted from your own context; the subscription you never use renewing tomorrow, caught; the report you promised in the group chat, ready to send. Everything is one click from firing through computer use, and nothing fires until you click.

Or click your Mac notch anytime and say "finish this for me." Sidekick takes over the thing you were doing with its own cursor while you move on.

On-device inference at this scale was supposed to be impossible: devices too slow, and models too dumb. So we built the stack ourselves: a custom LiteRT-LM fork (KV-cache reuse, speculative decoding, custom k-quants) that runs nightly on 8 GB Macs. The user's hardware does ~90% of the compute, and their own ChatGPT or Claude subscription does the rest, so our marginal cost is ~$0, and our servers store nothing.

Our alpha soft-launch was top post of the month on r/macapps (688 upvotes), and we launched to 4000+ users in our first week with $0 marketing. We're free and open source for consumers; the same engine on the work stack (Slack, Granola, Linear, Notion) is the enterprise business.

Sentient OS raised ~$1M in pre-seed, backed by YC, Afore, and the a16z Speedrun scout fund.
one_liner: On-device AI that knows your entire life and does your work overnight.

name: Simulithic
long_description: Simulithic continuously uses your production product like your real users do. We learn representative user journeys and run user simulations across different devices, browsers, account states, and environments to find failures that traditional scripted end-to-end tests miss.
one_liner: AI users that test your app on every device and browser

name: ChemPilot.ai
long_description:
We use AI and quantum-based simulations to discover and develop new materials for defense and dual-use applications, from energetics and propellants to carbon fibers, polymers, coatings and composites. Developing a new material today takes 10+ years of trial-and-error lab work. We compress that to months, using physics-based simulation, machine learning and AI agents that only send labs candidates that can actually be made.

Sam, Ofir and Maor have spent the past two years researching the discovery of these exact materials together at the Technion lab of our CSO, Prof. Alon Grinberg Dana (former MIT postdoc), working directly with defense primes and government R&D agencies. Together we bring deep expertise in chemical engineering, computational chemistry and AI, and the production systems to put them to work. ChemPilot spun out of that work.

The defense and dual-use industrial base runs on materials with fragile, sole-source and often adversarial supply chains, from energetics and propellants to carbon fibers, high-temperature composites and specialty polymers. Demand for new capabilities is surging, and materials take decades to develop. The West needs new materials it can make securely, fast and cheap - ChemPilot will help find and develop them.
one_liner: Discover novel defense related materials/molecules.

name: Veeza AI
long_description: Billions of people need tourist visas to travel the world. We use AI agents to prepare applications, verify documents, secure appointments, and handle the visa process end to end.
one_liner: AI tourist visa agent for people with weak passports.

name: Petrichor
long_description: Real biology requires a wet lab, and building one takes years and a team most AI companies don't have. Petrichor runs their experiments at scale and sends back the dense, clean data their models need to learn from.
one_liner: Wet lab infrastructure that turns AI experiments into training data.

name: Kailash Labs
long_description:
The world generates petabytes of video every day, and almost none of it is readable to machines.  Frontier VLMs that can unlock this (like Gemini) are too expensive to run at the volume real industries have, too generic for any single task, and can't be deployed on-prem where sensitive video lives.

We are building an auto vision factory: take video plus a customer's objective, distill a frontier model, and post-train a small open model that is SOTA on that one task and serve it blazingly fast. Our first product, Marlin, is a 2B-parameter open-weights video VLM that matches Gemini-2.5-flash on dense captioning and temporal grounding at a fraction of the cost.
one_liner: A factory for small and specialized video reasoning models

name: Saccade
long_description:
Alzheimer's testing today is bottlenecked around the onset of symptoms, when the damage is already done. Current treatments, including the FDA-approved drugs released in 2024, don't reverse the disease; they only slow it down. Earlier detection means earlier intervention.

Eye movement changes linked to Alzheimer's surface sooner than any other biomarker, up to 15 years before symptoms appear.

We deliver a 15-minute VR assessment delivered to patients in longevity clinics:
• Tasks: patients perform visual tasks designed by neurologists to trigger a distinct oculomotor response in people with Alzheimer's or on its path
• Hardware: our patent-pending attachment connects to any VR headset on the market and captures these eye movement patterns.
• Analysis: the patterns are compared against our ML model to produce a risk analysis.

Once classified, patients can access new interventions, such as the FDA-approved drugs. They're also referred to longevity practices, neurology practices or both, depending on their stage of decline.

Testing for the earliest biomarkers allows the earliest possible intervention. In some cases, that slows the disease enough that patients outlive the onset of symptoms and never face memory loss in their lifetime.
one_liner: World's Earliest Test for Alzheimer's Biomarkers

name: Agent 37
long_description:
* Ready to Use Instantly: Skip the complex server setup. It comes pre loaded with top AI Agents (like Claude Code and Hermes) so your agents can start working immediately.

* Keep Your Work Safe: Unlike other systems that delete everything when they finish a task, these sandboxes remember your files, code, and settings forever until you delete them.

* Pay Only for What You Use: Stop paying for idle servers. You pay a tiny fee to store your files, but you only pay for compute power during the exact minutes your AI is actively running.

* Zero Infrastructure Headaches: You don’t need to be a senior DevOps engineer or manage complex cloud networks. One simple command handles the entire backend for you.

* Connect to Any App: Allow your AI agents to securely log into and interact with everyday tools like Slack, Gmail, and GitHub in just a few clicks.
one_liner: Persistent sandboxes for agents like hermes, openclaw, claude code

name: Faraday
long_description:
Faraday builds industrial AI that learns how enterprises operate and executes long-horizon, multi-step tasks from the back office to the shop floor.

We sit on top of fragmented systems of record, coordinating work across existing software and teams. We combine operating procedures, enterprise data, and expert feedback to capture the rules and judgment behind complex processes. In customer-specific RL environments, we optimize the agent harness around each company’s systems, constraints, approvals, and exceptions.

We’re connecting to industrial hardware to bring live production data into the same feedback loop. Human corrections, machine data, and operating results help improve how agents plan and execute future work.
one_liner: Agents running industrial enterprises from back office to shop floor

name: Viraj Aero
long_description:
Viraj Aero builds gas turbines that deliver both power and cooling water for data centers. It needs no grid connection and no water pipeline.

Burning natural gas already produces water. Our patented system captures that water from the exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest is turned into steam and injected back into the turbine. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel (cheaper compute) and cuts NOx emissions by up to 99%, which cuts permit approvals from years to weeks.

We're building a genset around our first-of-its-kind gas turbine. It fits in a 10-foot container and runs anywhere, even in the desert. That matters because two-thirds of new data centers are being built in water-stressed regions.

We first built this steam-injected turbine for aircraft, where carrying water tanks isn't an option and efficiency is critical. We're currently integrating our full-scale prototype into an aircraft. The team comes from GE, Rolls-Royce and Formula 1, and we're already working with Safran, one of the world's largest aircraft engine manufacturers.
one_liner: Next generation gas turbines for data centers & aviation

name: Boat
long_description:
**Problem**

Humans used to need laptops to do their work. Now they prompt agents instead, and those agents need computers too: always-on, in large quantities, and with unlimited capabilities. 

Building and maintaining that yourself is far from trivial.

**Solution**

Boat provides powerful, simple, permissive Ubuntu VMs in the cloud. In a sandbox, an agent can work for long periods on code or on knowledge work like legal, research, reporting, and auditing.

**Why Boat and not any other cloud VM?**

1. It is ready out of the box: every sandbox ships with a desktop, chrome, languages, docker, snapshots, and templates, plus a CLI, SDK, API, and control pane for your fleet.
2. It is permissive and paradigm agnostic: any number of agents can use any number of sandboxes. Agents can run inside or use sandboxes as an external tool.
3. It is expertly crafted: we manage everything from the individual CPU to the orchestration software, which makes sandboxes stable, persistent, scalable, and secure.
4. It is the best performance and price in town: our CPUs rank first on HPC benchmarks, and sandboxes are typically 9x to 18x cheaper than other leading sandboxes.

**Further notes**

Sandboxes are hosted in Europe, which keeps prices low, and more regions are coming. Unless compliance requires it, agents don't notice the region they run in.
one_liner: The best cloud VMs for billions of agents

long_description: Applied Kinetics builds and deploys specialized AI employees to handle the coordination work behind America's energy and data center buildout. Our agents chase suppliers, track equipment approvals and delivery dates, and flag delays so project teams can keep critical equipment moving without hunting for updates across emails and spreadsheets.

name: Stacktrace

Stacktrace is the control layer for every agent: it sees every action, detects risky behavior, enforces the bounds your team sets, and steps in when an agent drifts from intent.
one_liner: See and control what your agents actually do

name: Altair Health
long_description:
Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions.

That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. 

Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so the longer we run a practice's billing, the better we predict what its insurers will pay, deny or delay.

We're building the default way a new practice gets paid: a doctor connects their EHR and bills clean from the first patient, completely self-serve and on auto-pilot.

Altair will be the financial platform every independent practice in America starts on and stays on.
one_liner: Stripe for medical billing

Founded by the former inference lead at Mistral AI, Munito is built on one belief: open and independent intelligence, both models and inference, is key to economic growth and prosperity.

Micora builds a solar-farm-in-a-box that can be shipped anywhere and built without specialized labor. We have designed a new type of solar farm micorgrid that is palletized, lightweight, and deployable. Our system autonomously builds 100kWp of capacity per day and is easily scalable to MWs of capacity which is a size currently only serviced by slow moving and at capacity EPCs. 

As demand from data centers, advanced manufacturing, and electrification strains existing power infrastructure, the ability to deploy substantial generation quickly is becoming increasingly valuable and unavailable. We are the only company that services utility-scale power needs in weeks.

name: Mirrors
long_description:
Production agents handle many different customer workflows. Currently, when one handles a situation badly, an engineer reads the trace and patches the prompt. The next situation needs another exception. Soon, improving the agent becomes a recurring engineering job, and the prompt keeps growing.

Mirrors finds patterns in past runs. Engineers review guidance for a specific situation and preview where it would apply. Mirrors then delivers that guidance while the agent works, inside the team’s existing setup. The team can check whether the change improved the outcome.

We’re building Mirrors for engineering teams running customer-facing agents across varied workflows, so they can improve behavior without hardcoding every lesson in the global prompt.
one_liner: Give AI agents the right context at the right moment

name: OnePatch
long_description: OnePatch is a forward-deployed AI SRE. It instruments your services, watches how they actually behave in prod, catches incidents, and drives each one to resolution. Think Datadog, except it doesn't stop at telling you something broke: it keeps going until the fix is shipped.

name: Asakana

Asakana does that entry instead: orders land in the ERP already entered, and anything unclear goes to a person before it goes in. Live at US seafood distributors today, returning 40%+ of order-desk time to selling. Founded by a seafood distributor and a Gemini builder.

name: Bryel

name: Elimentary

Elimentary’s is building AI agents that can run middle/back-office operations for private capital managers, starting with structured credit. Most private capital managers focus primarily on sourcing and capital deployment. Meanwhile post-investment operations receive step-child treatment. While AUMs have increased exponentially over the last decade, operations continue to be painfully supported by humans using spreadsheets and emails. Things have started to break leading to investment write-offs, fines, penalties, and sometimes lost LP relationships. 

Our agents can run these operations (borrowing base calcs, cracking loan tapes, NAV calculations, etc.) end to end autonomously. For one of our customers, our agents cut a 20-hour ops process to 30 minutes. It saved 90% of the manual hours, translating to $150k in annual savings.

name: Agent Relay

Agent Relay lets software teams' AI coding agents message each other directly, so people stop copy/pasting between Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and their teammates' agents. A frontend agent can ask the backend agent what an API returns, two agents can sort out a merge conflict between themselves, and your agent can answer a colleague's agent while you sleep.
 
Agents connect wherever they run: terminals, desktop apps, phones, laptops, cloud boxes, or a Mac mini across the world. Every session goes into shared, searchable history, so decisions don't get stuck in one person's chat. You can even let a customer's agent debug with yours. Setup takes about 5 minutes: give your agent the link and it installs itself. Use our hosted version free, or self-host the open-source version

name: Invertix
long_description:
The next constraint is not intelligence, it is the energy and operational cost of running it.
We deploy custom AI models inside critical infrastructure companies that ingest SCADA data, work orders, human interventions,  operational data no public model has seen, grounded in physics-informed neural networks and differentiable simulators. 
This creates a flywheel: more operator data → better process understanding → more efficient operations → cheaper energy → cheaper AI → more deployment → more data. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0uDH6pMn5OE

AI compute doubles every 2.2 years. Data center demand grows from 415 to 945 TWh by 2030. Without near-zero energy cost, AI remains limited by human infrastructure. We are the layer that runs AI at zero energy cost.
Energy is a $10 trillion market. The infrastructure layer doesn't exist yet. 
We are building it.
one_liner: Energy Superintelligence, AI that operates critical infrastructure

name: sintem

Open Actuation designs motors and actuators around your robot's unique form factor and mission - then we rapidly bring them to life with proprietary software and tooling geared for high-mix machining and assembly. We've designed and built motors for top drone OEMs and can assemble thousands of motors per month at our first factory in LA.

We're doing for motion components what 3D printing has done for structural components. This enables hardware teams to build and iterate at the speed of software so they can create elegant, reliable, ROI-positive robots and win massive markets.

name: Hemlock
long_description:
Every serious robotics lab is bottlenecked on the same thing: demonstration data. The field has converged on egocentric video and hand pose as the substrate, and both are now cheap to collect at scale. What neither of them contains is force. A video of someone picking up an egg and a video of someone picking up a rock are nearly identical in pixel space and nearly identical in joint angles. They differ almost entirely in a quantity nobody is recording. Policies trained without it learn geometry and inherit no sense of touch.

Hemlock closes that gap at the source. Our device, the Bracelet, is a wrist-worn surface EMG band that reads the electrical activity of the forearm muscles that actually drive the hand, which means it recovers contraction force directly rather than inferring it from motion. This distinction is the whole thesis: force cannot be reconstructed downstream of kinematics, because a hand squeezing hard isometrically and a hand resting can occupy the identical pose. Muscle signal is the only non-invasive channel that separates them.
one_liner: Force-sensing wristband for training robotic AI

Graphide keeps a live graph of the modules, classes, functions, etc. how they connect, and what each agent is touching as it works. Graphide then checks their changes against your architecture, making sure your agents are implementing what you had in mind.
one_liner: A graph based IDE for when agents program faster than you can read

name: Sutrix

Paying research teams at HSS, Emory, and Mount Sinai cut data prep from 3 weeks per study to 4 days, and now they are able to deliver tailored patient outcomes faster.

We built Sutrix because we lived this problem. Ritvik ran clinical research at HSS and Emory, and Supratik previously founded Kairo (a16z Speedrun, exited) and was an engineer at Amazon.

(2) Scheduling: what runs when, and who works on what. (3) Allocation: which warehouse or store gets each order. (4) Routing: boat, plane or truck, and which route each one takes. Founded out of MIT's Operations Research Center.

name: Papaya

Engineers don't have time to continually improve the agents they've shipped — the context bloat, overly chatty subagents, and broken tool calls sit in production traces nobody reads, quietly hurting agent efficiency. With Papaya they connect their agent directly via SDK, get actionable recommendations on how to improve quality, latency, and cost, and the ones they approve are pushed to production as pull requests.

Papaya runs 200+ research-backed analyses across context, prompts, prompt caching, subagents, and tool calls. Every recommendation is ranked by impact and comes with the production runs that produced it — typically a 10%+ quality improvement on the first workflow analysis.

name: Caveman

name: Acyclic Labs
long_description:
Acyclic builds the infrastructure for agent swarms: open-source primitives for running agents in parallel, and a managed agents platform that runs swarms for you. Complex, long-running tasks are split across many agents, each working in its own instant fork of the workspace, and finish in a fraction of the time.

We built Acyclic because we believe there are huge gains to be had in how agents are run, beyond the models themselves. Agents can already do real work, but they still do it one step at a time, so complex tasks take hours or days. Running them as swarms is an infrastructure problem: isolating each agent, dividing the work, and merging the results without conflicts. Today, teams use Acyclic to run heavy document-processing pipelines in minutes instead of hours.

At Cambridge, we researched ML and auto-parallelising compilers, and then we built multi-agent systems in production: Ram as a Palantir FDE for pharma clients, shipping systems for clinical trial design, and Varun leading agent architecture at Tracelight for Big 4 accounting firms. We kept asking the same question: the agents were good enough, so why couldn't we run thousands of them at once to make everything faster and cheaper? Acyclic is our answer.
one_liner: Agent swarms that make long-running tasks exponentially faster

one_liner: Humanoids to restock retail shelves & pick orders

name: Ascenix
long_description:
Ascenix is the all-in-one incident platform that turns unstructured EHR data into automated reporting, reimbursement recovery, compliance flagging, and clinical insight. We’re already live in 50 homes and scaling across North America. We connect to systems like PointClickCare and analyze the notes nurses already write, adapting to any note structure and any compliance or reporting requirement.

We help teams identify documentation gaps, uncover missed revenue opportunities and spot emerging resident risks, while reducing time spent reviewing charts and building spreadsheets. Our goal is to improve residents’ quality of life by helping care homes reach their full clinical, financial and operational potential.
one_liner: Clinical intelligence layer for skilled nursing facilities.

name: GrayPass
long_description:
Login tells you who signed in. GrayPass verifies the expected person is still in control before consequential actions happen. We use cognitive biometrics like typing rhythm, cursor movement, scrolling, and response timing alongside session and device context to continuously establish assurance.

Before actions like approving a payment, changing admin permissions, exporting sensitive data, or letting an AI agent act on someone’s behalf, GrayPass returns allow, challenge, hold, or deny and produces signed proof tied to that action.
one_liner: Verify that the expected person is in control before key actions.

name: Cyclon
long_description: Cyclon is rebuilding the phone around AI. Instead of opening apps and tapping through screens, you tell your phone what you want and it does it for you. With one touch, you can spin up AI agents to control your phone or handle tasks in the background. AI isn’t just inside an app - it’s the phone itself.
one_liner: a phone where AI is the interface

name: Ageospatial
long_description:
Ageospatial helps organizations value the risk on their physical assets (properties, land, infrastructure) remotely using satellite imagery.

97% of commercial properties are never physically inspected because it's too slow and expensive. So insurers price risk based on what the client or broker tells them, and about half the time at least one of those records is wrong. The result is mispricing, fraud, and an estimated $36B in premium leakage every year in the US alone, which gets exposed the moment a disaster hits.

Upload a list of addresses and their GeoAI reads satellite and street-level imagery, maps, real-time data, public records and the insurer's own data to determine what's really there, which natural and human hazards surround it, what changed over time, and which properties are worth inspecting. Each property becomes a living record that underwriting, claims and pricing teams can trace from past to present. Ageospatial deploys inside carriers and MGAs as an AI-native service, so insurers get outcomes delivered.
one_liner: Physical intelligence for every decision with Geospatial AI.

name: HABU
long_description:
HABU is an AI-native real estate development firm that helps real estate investors deploy capital to build housing faster, at lower cost, and with higher yield. 

We're building an internal AI-native operating system that completes 90%+ of development tasks at 95% faster processing speeds while delivering the same outcomes customers expect externally: high yield, low risk projects. We're selling the outcome, not the inputs to the outcome. 

Developers are service providers for white-collar investors: they find land, construct buildings, and operate and sell them for a profit. Our customers don't care how the projects are sourced or managed, only that they are completed on time and produce the forecasted returns. 

We use agentic workflows, geospatial analysis and mapping, and development-specific workflow automation to manage the end-to-end process. The result is 5x more projects per FTE compared to a non-AI developer, 20% faster project schedules, and 10-15% lower total project costs. 

We're *not* long term property owners, strictly the service provider (fee/merchant developer).

$160B was deployed into multifamily in 2025 and $534B into commercial real estate overall. Developers naturally have high operating margins and we are building to be the most operationally and capital efficient developer in the country. 

Starting first with multifamily in Phoenix and then expanding nationally.
one_liner: Like Crosby, but for real estate development

name: The Agentic Data Co.
long_description: We design and collect audio datasets for training speech models.
one_liner: Training Data For Speech Models.

name: Redoubt Insurance
long_description: Redoubt is a commercial insurance agency for small businesses. We believe our customers are our most important business partners, and they deserve our full attention. Machines can already handle the boring parts, the next step is to continually learn from experience.
one_liner: Commercial insurance for small businesses

name: Lark
long_description: Lark deploys AI agents that automate manual workflows for wholesale distributors, everything from customer quotes to inventory managment. Our agents work with existing ERP systems, learning from each distributor’s historical data and the team’s decisions. Together, these agents can run a distributor’s entire operation.
one_liner: Lark - AI agents that automate workflows for wholesale distributors

name: Hundred
long_description:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up consumer devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-millimeter cosmetic defects before parts reach the assembly line. 

In the consumer electronics industry, designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. 

The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.
one_liner: 100% automated inspection for consumer electronics parts

name: Tilo
long_description:
Tilo is a Linux-based operating system built for AI agents to work alongside people. On Tilo, computer use is up to 15x cheaper than on a normal OS.

Today agents use computers the way people do. They take screenshots and click through apps, which is slow, expensive, and brittle. In Tilo, every app exports actions, so agents work over MCP while people use the UI. You still see what each agent does in your apps, and anything it changes can be undone.

Any number of people and agents can work in one workspace in real time, across apps. Tilo runs as your OS, in our cloud, or headless on your machine, and you can open and share any workspace from the browser.
one_liner: A Linux-based, AI-native operating system.

name: OpenHack
long_description: OpenHack is an always on AI Security Engineer. OpenHack understands your business, system design and developer intent like a real security engineer. It ingests all this context to find the hardest vulnerabilities through AI codebase scanning, AI pentesting and Supply Chain Security. It verifies and prioritizes vulnerabilities automatically, and filters out false positives like a real security engineer drastically reducing overhead.
one_liner: Always-on AI security engineer

name: Sintropix
long_description: Autonomous accounting platform for global companies. We close your books and give you financial clarity while you run your business.
one_liner: Autonomous accounting platform for global companies

name: Adside.ai
long_description: We're Robin Choy and Guillaume Miara, founders of Adside (adside.ai). We're building Adside, a swarm of agents that manages ads on Meta, Google and LinkedIn, etc. We’re building the service we wished we had in our previous B2B marketing software company that we sold earlier this year.
one_liner: AI agency that manages paid ads on Meta, Google, LinkedIn, etc.

name: RATLOG
one_liner: Reusable heavy-lift rockets

name: Maritime
long_description: Maritime is a fully managed cloud platform for startups selling AI agents. We help them run thousands of agents, each in its own isolated, persistent computer, starting at $1 per agent per month, with all underlying infrastructure, scaling, sleep/wake, and monitoring handled automatically.
one_liner: The managed cloud for AI agents.

name: DeepMark
long_description: DeepMark is the authentication layer for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we embed a compact, machine-readable ID directly into the audio, not in metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. The ID resolves to a trust record, so a bank, a call center, or the person on the line can verify in real time who the agent is.
one_liner: A live watermark inside AI voice that survives phone calls

name: Boxes.dev
long_description: Port your development environment to the cloud. Give every coding agent on its own cloud computer, bring your Codex or Claude subscription, start agents from Slack and Linear, and manage them from your desktop, phone, or terminal.
one_liner: Cloud development environments for AI coding

name: Mantle
long_description:
Mantle is a full-stack field service company that deploys, fixes and maintains machines for the companies that build them. We're not a marketplace or software tool, we own uptime directly to provide better, more reliable service without burdening your engineers on support calls. 

$500B+ a year is spent to keep machines running in the US, we're coming for all of it.
one_liner: The pit crew for machines and robots.

name: Keres
long_description: Keres (KAIR-eez) builds reusable unmanned jet interceptors for air defense. The Garmur launches on cue, closes at jet speed, positively identifies and kills drones and cruise missiles, then lands to fly again. It gives commanders a fighter-class response at a fraction of the cost.
one_liner: Kill the drone, keep the jet. Reusable unmanned interceptors.
